note: Product-neutral fixtures for registries/operating-model/context-manifest.schema.json and scripts/lib/context-manifest.mjs. Every `valid` record must pass evaluateContextManifest with no problem; every `invalid` record must produce at least one. One model everywhere: each record declares $schema = ../../registries/operating-model/context-manifest.schema.json — a portable relative reference that, resolved INSIDE THE MERIDIAN NAMESPACE, lands exactly on the specialised schema (which composes the reused scoped-record envelope with the body). The manifest belongs to EXACTLY ONE run and the link is DETERMINISTIC: execution_run_ref, task_specification_ref and human_control_ref are CLOSED structured pinned references { record_type, id, reference, run_id?, revision?/sha256? }; scope.id equals execution_run_ref.id by exact string comparison; human_control_ref.run_id equals execution_run_ref.id; task_specification_ref carries no run_id. run_state_checkpoint is the PINNED authoritative snapshot; it is NOT proven by a second copy of the same fields inside the manifest. Every pinned reference — the manifest's and the checkpoint's — is RESOLVED through the companion `resolution` set (kept outside every manifest.spec), and the checkpoint's scope_revision, lifecycle_stage, work_status, next_action, next_gate, blocker_ids, resolved_norms and completed_checks are checked against the state the RESOLVED execution-run record carries. A fabricated sha256, and a coordinated edit of both the manifest copy and the checkpoint copy, are rejected because the resolved record is the anchor. The manifest's scope_revision, next step, next gate, blocker-id set and completed-check set must still equal the checkpoint's, and the set of applicable_norms references must equal run_state_checkpoint.resolved_norms (the manifest adds a rationale, never substitutes the set). An exact revision is a closed set: a full Git SHA (40 or 64 hex), a strict v?X.Y.Z tag, or a SHA-256 digest. A branch or channel reference (a slash, a bare word, or a known moving token) is floating whatever digits it carries; any other provider-specific or unknown revision form is weak and needs a sha256 — the same rule for pinned references, applicable norms and mutable sources. An unbounded material dump and a full evidence / handoff / field-evaluation field are rejected by construction. No rooted machine path, no file:// and no product literals anywhere.
resolution_note: The companion record-resolution set, kept OUTSIDE every manifest.spec. scripts/lib/context-manifest.mjs (makeRecordResolver) turns this into the (pinnedRef) => resolvedEntry resolver the gate and the standalone set pass to evaluateContextManifest. Keyed by the reference each pinned_ref carries. Each entry is the transformer's confirmed view of ONE edition and its shape is a CLOSED contract — a missing required field is a precise error, never a skipped comparison: record_type and a non-empty id are required; reference, when stated, must equal the resolved reference; at least one of revision / content_digest (a synthetic stand-in here for the SHA-256 over the resolved source) is required; an execution-run entry MUST carry resolved_state with task_specification_ref, scope_revision, lifecycle_stage, work_status, next_action, next_gate, blocker_ids, resolved_norms and completed_checks (the run's OWN state that run_state_checkpoint must reproduce); a run-human-control entry MUST carry linked_run_ref (the run it belongs to). BOTH the manifest's references and the checkpoint's own references are resolved through this set: the checkpoint axes are checked against the run resolved from run_state_checkpoint.execution_run_ref, and that must be the same edition as the manifest's top-level execution_run_ref. A fabricated digest, a coordinated edit of both in-document copies, or a checkpoint pointing at a different real record all fail because this set is the anchor.
